clusters.name: Cluster C (Anxious/Fearful)
items: Avoids occupational activities involving significant interpersonal contact due to fear of criticism/rejection
Unwilling to get involved with people unless certain of being liked
Shows restraint within intimate relationships due to fear of being shamed or ridiculed
Preoccupied with being criticized or rejected in social situations
Inhibited in new interpersonal situations because of feelings of inadequacy
Views self as socially inept, personally unappealing, or inferior to others
Unusually reluctant to take personal risks or engage in new activities due to fear of embarrassment

criteria.thresholds: >=4/7 criteria starting by early adulthood (DSM p.764-765)
subtypes: Section III Alternative Model: Anxiousness, Withdrawal, Anhedonia, Intimacy Avoidance (DSM p.885-886)

epidemiology.sex_ratio: Slightly higher in women in community surveys; equal in Synopsis (DSM p.766, Synopsis ch.19)
epidemiology.onset_age_typical: Childhood shyness escalating during adolescence and early adulthood (DSM p.766-767)
epidemiology.prognosis: Tends to attenuate or remit with age (0.8% prevalence above age 65) (DSM p.767)

etiology.genetic: Cluster C genetic vulnerability to anxiety and harm avoidance (Synopsis ch.19)
etiology.neurobiology: High Harm Avoidance (HA), High Reward Dependence (RD), Low Novelty Seeking (NS) (Cloninger model; Synopsis ch.19)
etiology.environmental: Insecure attachment (preoccupied/fearful), insensitive or traumatized parenting (DSM p.766, Dulcan p.525)

items: Schizoid PD: AvPD craves companionship but fears rejection; Schizoid has no desire/enjoyment in relationships (DSM p.742, 767)
Social Anxiety Disorder: AvPD features a pervasive entrenched view of self as socially inept/inferior and broader avoidance (DSM p.767)
Dependent PD: AvPD avoids social proximity due to fear of rejection; Dependent seeks proximity and submission (DSM p.767)
Agoraphobia: AvPD is motivated by fear of rejection/shame; Agoraphobia by fear of panic/physical harm (DSM p.767)
Paranoid PD: AvPD reluctance to confide is due to fear of embarrassment/inadequacy, not malicious intent (DSM p.767)
key_numbers: >=4 of 7 criteria required for DSM-5-TR diagnosis (DSM p.764)
5.2% prevalence in NCS-R Part II (DSM p.766)
2.1% median prevalence across 6 epidemiological studies (DSM p.766)
0.8% prevalence in adults over 65 years (DSM p.767)

first_line: CBT with gradual in vivo exposure (Synopsis ch.19)
Coping Cat / SET-C protocols for pediatric social anxiety/avoidance (Dulcan p.334, 971-972)
Assertiveness training and Group therapy (Synopsis ch.19)
second_line: SSRIs (Sertraline, Fluoxetine) for rejection sensitivity and comorbid anxiety/depression (Synopsis ch.19, Dulcan p.330)
Beta-blockers (Atenolol, Propranolol) for autonomic hyperarousal during social exposure (Synopsis ch.19)
key_side_effects: Behavioral activation, insomnia, motor restlessness, and suicidal ideation risk in youth SSRI initiation (Dulcan p.249, StahlKids p.285)
treatment.monitoring: Monitor weekly for activation/suicidality at start; full trial 8-12 weeks; continue 12 months after response (Dulcan p.331)

high_yield: Crucial distinction from Schizoid PD: AvPD deeply craves human companionship ('desire for companionship') but is paralyzed by fear of rejection (DSM p.767, Synopsis ch.19)
Differs from Social Anxiety Disorder by an entrenched, pervasive view of self as globally inferior/socially inept (DSM p.767)
Cloninger temperament profile: High Harm Avoidance (HA), High Reward Dependence (RD), Low Novelty Seeking (NS) (Synopsis ch.19)
CBT warning: Uncontrolled exposure tasks that end in failure can reinforce fragile self-esteem (Synopsis ch.19)
Pediatric CAMS trial benchmark: Sertraline + CBT achieved 81% response rate vs 60% CBT alone (Dulcan p.330-331)
